sources.title: A catalogue of Trump's attacks on judges, prosecutors and witnesses

frozen_original.synopsis: Throughout 2023, Donald Trump posted dozens of attacks on Truth Social targeting special counsel Jack Smith, witnesses in his criminal cases, and judges presiding over them. Trump called Smith deranged and a thug and attacked witnesses by name. The posts prompted Smith to seek protective gag orders citing witness intimidation concerns. Legal experts warned the public attacks constituted unprecedented obstruction behavior and that any other defendant would face contempt charges for similar conduct.
frozen_original.title: Trump Posts Dozens of Attacks on Prosecutors, Witnesses, and Judges

proposal.description_long: In August 2023, prosecutors in the federal election case against Donald Trump asked a judge in Washington to impose a protective order governing the use and disclosure of discovery materials. The Justice Department argued that public disclosure of evidence such as grand-jury interviews or sealed-warrant materials could chill witnesses or affect the administration of justice. The filing cited Trump’s history of social media posts about judges, lawyers and witnesses in his cases, including a Truth Social message stating, “If you go after me, I’m coming after you.” Trump’s defense described the post as political speech and contested the request. This procedural request concerned access to evidence exchanged in discovery; it was not itself a gag order covering all public statements and did not establish that the posts were criminal conduct. Other reporting in September 2023 described a separate request to restrict statements about participants in the election case. The supplied Washington Post link is an October 2023 catalogue, but its article body was not readable in the focused review. The revised title and account describe the documented protective-order request and avoid an unsupported count of “dozens” or a legal conclusion about obstruction. A final order should be consulted before describing the precise restrictions imposed.
proposal.description_medium: In August 2023, special counsel Jack Smith asked the court in Washington to restrict how Donald Trump and his lawyers could disclose materials received in discovery in the 2020 election case. Prosecutors cited Trump’s history of posting about people involved in his cases and pointed to a Truth Social post reading, “If you go after me, I’m coming after you.” Trump’s lawyers argued the post was political speech. The filing documents the prosecutors’ request and stated concern, not a judicial finding that the posts constituted obstruction or witness intimidation.
proposal.description_short: Prosecutors cited Trump’s social media posts in seeking a discovery protective order in the 2020 election case; the filing was not a finding that the posts were crimes.
